en.title: Do Static Door-Handle Shocks Only Happen in Winter?
en.description:
Static electricity cannot be explained by winter versus summer alone. Dry conditions usually favor charge accumulation; moisture helps charge dissipate more quickly. Materials and the conditions of contact and separation also affect charging. Charging still occurs at high humidity. Taiwanese winters are not assumed to be dry, nor summers free of static. This short only explains a static scenario in which a charged body meets a conductor at a different potential and rapid charge transfer may occur. It is neither inevitable nor fixed in direction and does not diagnose actual leakage at a handle. Diagrams are not to scale; no humidity measurements or body-discharge experiments. The 35–55-second duration is an estimate, not a synthesized timing.

Sources directly checked 2026-10-01: EOS/ESD Association, Part 1 An Introduction to ESD (page marked ©2020, not an update date), and US NWS, Lightning and Thunder Experiments, dry-air/moisture explanation (no publication/update date shown). No experimental instructions or voltage tables are used.

en.title: Behind Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V: Why Two Steps? | So That's Why
en.description:
This episode focuses on two-step text editing. In Tesler's account, NLS commands generally named the action before the object; he and colleagues explored selecting text before issuing a command. Gypsy offered separate cut/copy and paste operations using dedicated keys. His article also describes an earlier two-step move in TVEDIT, so the whole concept cannot be credited to one person. Today's Microsoft documentation lists Ctrl+C/V for text editing, while Apple's Mac uses Command-C/V. Function tables do not establish why those letters were originally chosen. Two steps separate source and destination choices; they do not guarantee support in every app or greater speed in every task. A design story, not a shortcut-settings tutorial.

Sources read directly on 2026-10-01: current Microsoft and Apple function descriptions, a mirrored PDF of Tesler's own 2012 article, and his oral history held by CHM. Recollections are a participant's perspective, not a complete priority-of-invention finding. The original letter explaining letter choices was not obtained: no claims about V's shape, neighboring keys or Lisa key-selection motives, or that PARC invented Ctrl+C/V. No historical software reconstruction, timing, media generation or audio/final-video QA. Original diagrams are conceptual.
